Score 0.5 only when small-entity-specific burden appears without certification/alternatives/outreach detail. Score 1.0 for IRFA/FRFA adequacy, certification validity, disproportionate impact, evaluated alternatives, or SBREFA outreach. Score 0.0 when RFA analysis is missing or inadequate.
105.orig_description: Compliance with RFA/SBREFA: prepare IRFA/FRFA or valid certification when rules may significantly affect a substantial number of small entities; assess disproportionate impacts; consider less‑burdensome significant alternatives; conduct SBREFA outreach as required; and document small‑entity impact tests and results.

106.best_description: Score only if the comment engages with the SEC climate-related disclosure rule (Items 1500–1508: governance, risk management/strategy, targets/scenario analysis, GHG Scopes 1–3, assurance, safe harbors, data tagging). Answer NA if the comment is about a different agency, docket, or topic entirely (e.g. tax, USDA, fisheries, immigration, general opposition/support with no climate-disclosure content) — do not score these 0.0. Once on-topic: 1.0 = addresses requirements accurately and substantively; 0.5 = partial/vague engagement; 0.0 = on-topic but substantively noncompliant or misstates the framework.
106.orig_description: Compliance with SEC climate disclosure framework: governance (Item 1501), risk management and strategy, targets/goals and scenario analysis, GHG inventory (Scopes 1–3 as applicable), assurance (Item 1506), safe harbors (Item 1507), and structured data tagging (Item 1508).

107.best_description: Score only comments about an exchange or SRO fee filing (e.g., market-data, transaction, or access fees). If the comment concerns a different topic, agency, or docket entirely, answer NA—not 0.0. Score 1.0 for precise service definitions, full fee schedules with effective-date/pro-ration mechanics, transparent cost allocation, competitive/cost-based justification, parity or reasoned differentials vs. peers, and clear escalation (e.g., CPI indexing). Score 0.5 if some but not most of these elements appear. Score 0.0 only when the filing is about fees but lacks these elements or justification.
107.orig_description: Quality of exchange/SRO fee filings: precise service definitions and functional changes; full fee schedules with effective‑date/pro‑ration mechanics; transparent shared‑cost allocation; competitive or cost‑based justifications; parity or reasoned differentials vs. peers; and clear escalation (e.g., CPI indexing).

108.best_description: Score ONLY comments whose visible text engages ICR/PRA burden: states need/use, names collections, or gives a concrete hours estimate. If visible text is only a cover letter/docket header, "see attached file(s)" with no burden content shown, or general policy/privacy commentary never addressing need, collections, or hours, answer NA, not 0.0. 1.0 = directly answers necessity/use AND gives a concrete burden estimate (e.g., actual hours), even without respondent breakdowns or opportunity-cost valuation. 0.5 = only one element, or vague estimates. 0.0 = engages ICR burden but omits nearly all required content.
108.orig_description: Paperwork Reduction Act compliance for ICRs: state need and intended use; identify all collections; provide standard burden breakdowns (respondent types/forms, counts, frequency, hours/time per response); estimate total annual burden; value burden hours as opportunity costs (not fees); document screened nonparticipants and program‑integrity/oversight burdens as applicable.

109.best_description: Define Generic ICR scopes and current‑action renewals/extensions; design and clear program‑specific collections (administrative data, surveys/interviews/observations); and establish ongoing quality metrics/reporting frameworks in coordination with OMB.
109.orig_description: Define Generic ICR scopes and current‑action renewals/extensions; design and clear program‑specific collections (administrative data, surveys/interviews/observations); and establish ongoing quality metrics/reporting frameworks in coordination with OMB.

110.best_description: Score whether the comment addresses use of EPA-approved drinking water analytical methods and/or compliance with sampling requirements (collection, preservation, containers, holding times) or special monitoring programs (e.g., UCMR, sodium), including QA/QC and documentation. Answer NA if the comment does not discuss SDWA analytical methods or sampling at all—including cover letters, docket submissions on unrelated rules (e.g., food labeling, fisheries), or text that only references an attached letter without stating its content. Score 0.0 only if the comment engages this topic but opposes, ignores, or fails required methods/sampling/QA-QC. Score 0.5 for partial or ambiguous compliance; 1.0 for clear, specific support of approved methods and sampling compliance.
110.orig_description: Use approved drinking water analytical methods and comply with sampling requirements (collection/preservation/containers/holding times, special monitoring programs such as UCMR and sodium), with appropriate QA/QC and documentation.

111.best_description: Assess accuracy characterizing the APA: rule/rulemaking definition; legislative vs. interpretive rules vs. policy statements; exemption/formal-rulemaking scope; CRA implications; when guidance becomes de facto rulemaking needing notice-and-comment. Score 1.0 for correct, specific analysis. Score 0.5 for partial analysis, process complaints, or arguments that voluntary standards should become binding rules. Score 0.0 when APA characterization is attempted and errs. Score NA when the comment narrates rulemaking history, describes substantive provisions, or requests an outcome with no explicit rule-type argument; also NA for pure policy content, extension requests, boilerplate letterhead, or illegible/attachment-only text.
111.orig_description: Accurate characterization of the APA: what constitutes a rule/rulemaking; distinctions among legislative rules, interpretive rules, and policy statements; scope/limits of APA exemptions and formal rulemaking triggers; CRA implications; and when guidance crosses into de facto substantive rulemaking warranting notice‑and‑comment.

112.best_description: Judge engagement with IFR/DFR or emergency/reopened-comment procedures: good-cause findings, effective/withdrawal dates, reopener scope, adverse-comment handling, post-promulgation commitments. Read all visible text, even if truncated or mostly letterhead. A request to extend or reopen the comment period (e.g., "extension request attached") IS engagement with reopener scope, even without further discussion. A bare docket citation or reference to another's letter is NOT engagement. Score 1.0 for clear engagement (including a clear extension/reopening request); 0.5 for partial/indirect; 0.0 only if it engages the topic poorly. NA if no engagement exists.
112.orig_description: Proper use and documentation of IFRs/DFRs and emergency/reopened comment notices: good‑cause findings, effective dates and withdrawal triggers, scope limits of reopeners, handling of adverse comments, and commitments to consider post‑promulgation input.

113.best_description: Quality and completeness of Unified Agenda/Regulatory Plan entries and tracker metadata, including required content, classifications (e.g., Long‑Term Actions), action type, and proper cross‑references to RegInfo.gov/Unified Agenda.
113.orig_description: Quality and completeness of Unified Agenda/Regulatory Plan entries and tracker metadata, including required content, classifications (e.g., Long‑Term Actions), action type, and proper cross‑references to RegInfo.gov/Unified Agenda.

114.best_description: Score comments on survey design, instrument quality, and sample representativeness: methodological plans; valid response scales/coding; appropriate collection modes; representative sample design; respondent notifications; split-sample experiments. 1.0 = substantive, concrete treatment of design/instrument/sampling. 0.5 = only brief or tangential mention (e.g., burden-hour estimates, collection frequency) without real design/instrument/sampling substance. NA = comment has no survey-methodology content at all (e.g., general opposition/support). Never score NA-eligible comments as 0.0; reserve 0.0 for comments that engage survey methodology but do so invalidly or unsoundly.
114.orig_description: Sound survey planning/design and administration: written methodological plans; valid, clear response scales and coding/transformations; appropriate modes; sample design ensuring representativeness; respondent notifications; and experimental split‑sample designs when used.

115.best_description: Score NA when the comment does not engage SEC disclosure rules: off-topic rants, form letters to other agencies (IRS, USDA, NOAA), or general opinions with no reference to disclosure items, forms, or regulations. Only score 0.0/0.5/1.0 when the comment actually discusses SEC-regulated disclosure content under Reg S-K, Reg AB, Reg M-A, or industry-specific instructions (definitions, content/presentation instructions, scaled disclosures, asset-level data, M-A items, exhibits, climate items incorporated by reference). Score 1.0 for full, correctly-scoped item compliance; 0.5 for partial/ambiguous engagement; 0.0 for clear noncompliance or misapplication.
115.orig_description: Ensure registrants satisfy applicable itemized SEC disclosure requirements across affected forms and regulations (Reg S‑K, Reg AB, Reg M‑A, and industry‑specific instructions), including definitions, content/presentation instructions, scaled disclosures, asset‑level data, M‑A items, exhibits, and any climate‑related items incorporated by reference.

116.best_description: Clarity and transparency around OIRA/OMB oversight: identify review stage as a distinct engagement point, disclose communications and changes made at OMB suggestion, satisfy agency regulatory plan/reporting requirements, and seek/process transparency and accountability in oversight records.
116.orig_description: Clarity and transparency around OIRA/OMB oversight: identify review stage as a distinct engagement point, disclose communications and changes made at OMB suggestion, satisfy agency regulatory plan/reporting requirements, and seek/process transparency and accountability in oversight records.

117.best_description: How an agency adopts/references technical standards: NTTAA voluntary-consensus preference, IBR compliance (1 CFR part 51), accurate/current citations. Score 1.0 only when the comment names a specific standard/code (e.g., ASTM, ISO, NFPA) and takes a position, flags it wrong/outdated, invokes IBR, or requests access — a docket number, RIN, or its own CFR section is NOT a standard. Score 0.5 only for a clear but unnamed reference to a technical standard. Answer NA — never 0.0 — for cover-letter/docket boilerplate, 'see attached' placeholders, general advocacy naming no standard, or unrelated content.
117.orig_description: Policies and mechanics for adopting/referencing technical standards: preference for voluntary consensus standards (NTTAA), incorporation by reference compliance (1 CFR part 51 reasonable availability), accurate/current citations and publication names, availability/accessibility of referenced materials, and agency‑specific recognition programs.

118.best_description: Score only comments that engage the ACA §156.130(e) premium adjustment percentage: its annual methodology (e.g., premium growth measure choice), calculation, or its application to cost-sharing/required contribution parameters. Answer NA if the comment does not discuss this topic at all (e.g., unrelated dockets, form cover letters, general opposition/support statements, off-topic personal stories) — do not score NA content as 0.0. Score 1.0 if the comment gives a substantive, specific methodology or parameter critique/proposal; 0.5 if it references the premium adjustment percentage or its application but only vaguely or partially; 0.0 if it explicitly addresses this topic but is substantively wrong, empty, or non-responsive.
118.orig_description: Maintain, update, and publish the annual premium adjustment percentage under §156.130(e), including methodology choices (e.g., premium growth measures) and application to related cost‑sharing and required contribution parameters.

119.best_description: Check whether the comment plans/conducts government-to-government Tribal consultation, maps operational areas affecting Tribal treaty or reserved rights, and documents Tribal impacts/consultations in the rulemaking record. Score 1.0 only if it describes a concrete consultation process plus mapping plus documentation. Score 0.5 if it addresses just one or two of these elements, or mentions them without specifics. Score 0.0 if it discusses Tribal rights or the rule's Tribal impact but omits consultation planning, mapping, or documentation entirely. Answer NA if the comment has no substantive text on Tribal consultation at all—e.g., a bare letterhead, forwarded attachment, cover letter, or 'see attached file' reference with no discussion of the topic itself.
119.orig_description: Plan and conduct government‑to‑government consultation, map operational areas affecting Tribal treaty or reserved rights, and document Tribal impacts and consultations in rulemaking records.

120.best_description: Score only comments discussing A-76 public-private cost comparisons. Check whether they include: base and administration costs; one-time conversion/transition and other incremental costs; accurate overhead/tax and space/parking/facility treatment (fair-rental valuation); correct labor benefit/retirement rates; and proper deductions/attribution per guidance. Give 1.0 if all elements are present and correct, 0.5 for minor gaps or errors, 0.0 if the comparison omits or misstates major elements. Answer NA if the comment does not address an A-76 cost comparison at all -- e.g., unrelated topics or general opinions with no cost content.
120.orig_description: Completeness and correctness of A‑76 cost comparisons: include base and administration costs; one‑time conversion/transition and other incremental costs; accurate overhead/tax and space/parking/facility cost treatments (fair‑rental valuation); correct labor benefit/retirement rates; and proper deductions/attribution consistent with guidance.

121.best_description: Score only discussion of THIS rule's own consultation/participation process: scope, outreach/notice, read-ahead materials, comment-period timing, records, public access to plans/decisions, contingency planning for participation itself, or pre-legislative consultation summaries. Exclude docket/address headers, empty "see attached" submissions, unrelated records-access complaints, commenters' own contingency plans, and substantive requirements like notification list-serves. Give 1.0 for substantive engagement—extension/meeting requests, clear complaints about this rule's notice, timing, or records—even if brief. Give 0.5 for vague mentions lacking clear stance. Give 0.0 when the comment explicitly calls this rule's process absent, inadequate, or refused. NA otherwise.
121.orig_description: Plan and execute public consultation with clear scope and outreach/notification methods; provide read‑ahead materials; maintain consultation records and public access to plans/decisions; ensure contingency planning for participation; and include required summaries of pre‑legislative consultation.

122.best_description: Agency practices for comment periods and participation: timely notices; topic‑limited solicitations and supplemental reopeners with clear scope; integrity protections (avoid identity theft/automated submissions); and clear filing links and calls to action.
122.orig_description: Agency practices for comment periods and participation: timely notices; topic‑limited solicitations and supplemental reopeners with clear scope; integrity protections (avoid identity theft/automated submissions); and clear filing links and calls to action.

123.best_description: Score only comments substantively about the 2015 CCR/coal ash rule under RCRA. Answer NA if the comment is generic (e.g., a content-free rant, boilerplate, or pure opposition/support with no subject-matter reference) and does not itself identify CCR, coal ash, or this rule as its topic — do not infer topic from context or docket. Score 0.0 if it names the CCR rule or coal ash but shows no engagement with applicability, planning, corrective action, or permitting. Score 0.5 for on-topic general support or opposition to coal ash protections without technical specifics. Score 1.0 for substantive engagement with applicability (including legacy impoundments), required plans (e.g., Inflow Design Flood control), groundwater corrective action, or site-specific permitting pathways.
123.orig_description: CCR regulatory compliance under RCRA: determine applicability (including legacy impoundments), develop required plans (e.g., Inflow Design Flood control systems), implement corrective actions to meet groundwater standards, and follow site‑specific permitting pathways.

124.best_description: Evaluate whether the comment engages with A-76 competitive-sourcing cost comparisons: establishing MEOs, benchmarking in-house vs. contractor performance, cost elements (capital/hidden costs), cost accounting, savings/ceilings documentation, lease justification, multi-function study scope, and A-76 policy compliance (e.g., no quotas). Score 1.0 for rigorous, complete, auditable comparisons; 0.5 for partial coverage; 0.0 if the comment addresses a make-or-buy/privatization/contracting-out decision but ignores or undermines cost-comparison rigor. Answer NA if the comment never raises make-or-buy, privatization, contracting-out, or in-house-vs-contractor issues at all.
124.orig_description: Evaluate make-or-buy decisions with complete, auditable A-76 cost comparisons: establish MEOs, benchmark in-house vs. contractor performance, include all relevant cost elements (e.g., cost of capital/hidden costs), ensure adequate cost accounting, document savings and ceilings, justify leases, scope multi-function studies appropriately, and comply with A-76 policies (e.g., no quotas).

125.best_description: Assess applicability and enforcement of A‑76 to commercial activities (and exclusions), restrictions on workarounds, required approvals for new in‑house starts, and implementation details and accommodations consistent with A‑76 policy.
125.orig_description: Assess applicability and enforcement of A‑76 to commercial activities (and exclusions), restrictions on workarounds, required approvals for new in‑house starts, and implementation details and accommodations consistent with A‑76 policy.

126.best_description: Score whether the comment uses firm bids solicited under procurement rules to build cost estimates, tells offerors an in-house estimate exists and award is uncertain, and keeps bids comparable to the government estimate. Score 1.0 if all elements are present; 0.5 if bids are used but one is missing or unclear. Score 0.0 only if the comment addresses commercial bids, cost estimates, or procurement pricing yet fails these criteria. Answer NA if the comment does not discuss commercial bidding or procurement cost estimation — never score unrelated topics as 0.0.
126.orig_description: Establish valid commercial cost estimates from firm bids or proposals solicited under procurement rules, informing offerors that an in‑house estimate is being developed and award is uncertain, and ensure comparability with government estimates.

127.best_description: Rate only comments discussing an agency's own internal ADP/IT management: new or revised systems and R&D projects, resource/cost tracking, productivity improvement plans and accomplishments, management-effectiveness goals, triggers for reporting new systems, or inter-directorate study coverage. Answer NA if the comment does not discuss internal ADP/IT management planning or reporting at all (e.g., it addresses an unrelated rule or topic, like fisheries, permitting, or other program substance). Answer 0.0 only if the comment does discuss internal ADP/IT management but omits required elements or provides no concrete planning/reporting content. Answer 1.0 if it substantively covers the required elements; 0.5 if it covers some but not all.
127.orig_description: Annual planning/reporting on ADP/IT: identify new/revised systems and R&D projects, resource/cost tracking, productivity improvement plans and accomplishments, management‑effectiveness goals, triggers for reporting new systems, and coverage of inter‑directorate study areas.

128.best_description: Score whether SEC filings meet itemized disclosure requirements under Regulation S-K, AB, or M-A (e.g., purposes/plans, ratings, solicitations/recommendations). Apply only when the comment addresses SEC filing content under these regs. Answer NA — not 0.0 — if the comment does not concern an SEC filing or these regulations (wrong agency/docket, unrelated topic, general opinion, no filing discussed). Score 1.0 if required items are fully addressed, 0.5 if partial/vague, 0.0 only when the comment discusses SEC filing disclosures but omits or violates required items.
128.orig_description: Filings meet itemized disclosure requirements across applicable SEC regulations (e.g., Regulation S‑K item disclosures, Regulation AB content, and Regulation M‑A items such as purposes/plans, ratings, and solicitations/recommendations).

129.best_description: Score whether the comment engages reasoned-decisionmaking substance: data, methods, alternatives, reliance interests, critique of the rule's rationale, or process/transparency adequacy (extension requests, notice or transparency challenges) — not mere jargon like 'NPRM.' 1.0 needs visible substantive text: data/expertise, weighed tradeoffs, alternatives proposed/rejected, or a specific causal critique — never from letterhead or 'see attached' alone. 0.5: mechanics facts without alternatives; a concrete reliance investment (dates/actions under prior uncertainty) behind a request; a bare process/transparency demand; or a transmittal with relevant letterhead but no visible substance. 0.0: opinion/personal-impact anecdote. NA if off-topic/unassessable.
129.orig_description: Rulemakings satisfy APA/agency procedures: timely/proper NPRM, logical outgrowth, disclosure of data/methods, reasoned explanation for changes and reliance interests, consideration/rejection of reasonable alternatives, and responses to significant comments (including direct‑final/interim‑final contexts).

130.best_description: Score any comment/notice naming this rulemaking via docket number, RIN, specific CFR part/section, or dated 'Re:'/Subject line. General policy talk with no such citation is NA — never infer a docket from topic alone. 1.0 = at least one correct identifier (agency, docket number, RIN, or CFR part) is present — do not require date, authority citation, summary, or participation instructions unless the item is itself a full agency notice. 0.5 = identifier attempted but ambiguous, partial, or minor error. 0.0 = identifier attempted but incorrect or missing.
130.orig_description: Notices/preambles comply with APA and FR requirements: required identifiers (agency, RIN/docket, CFR parts), authority citations, concise summaries/metadata, statement of terms/substance or subjects/issues, participation instructions, filing citations/availability, and correct amendment/format conventions.

131.best_description: Determine EO applicability and conformance (e.g., EO 12866/13563/14192 planning and review, transparency about OMB/OIRA review status) and address EO‑based consultation/analysis expectations as relevant.
131.orig_description: Determine EO applicability and conformance (e.g., EO 12866/13563/14192 planning and review, transparency about OMB/OIRA review status) and address EO‑based consultation/analysis expectations as relevant.

132.best_description: Score only comments containing quantitative PRA/ICR burden content: respondent counts, frequency, hours per response, total hours, or wage/cost figures. Answer NA when none appear: opinions on a requirement's reasonableness, anecdotes, seconding another commenter's stance without new figures, naming/describing a provision, letterhead citing an ICR title, boilerplate, "see attached" stubs, unrelated "collection" senses. Answer 0.0 only when the comment gives or disputes burden figures that are incomplete, unsubstantiated, or contested. 0.5 for partial numeric estimates; 1.0 only for complete, objective figures covering every required element per provision.
132.orig_description: Identify each PRA‑covered information collection and provide objective, transparent burden estimates (respondent counts, frequency, hours per response, total hours) and where relevant associated wage/cost estimates for each provision, for submission to OMB.

133.best_description: PRA notices include all required elements (e.g., affected public, legal authority, burden estimates, change descriptions) and properly solicit public comment on PRA‑specified topics and itemized ICRs subject to OMB review.
133.orig_description: PRA notices include all required elements (e.g., affected public, legal authority, burden estimates, change descriptions) and properly solicit public comment on PRA‑specified topics and itemized ICRs subject to OMB review.

134.best_description: Answer NA unless the text engages a PRA information collection request (ICR): paperwork burden, OMB approval, forms, or a collection notice. General policy opinions, personal stories, or unrelated comments are NA, never 0.0. Score 1.0 when it covers identifying the collection PLUS necessity, burden estimate, concrete reduction methods (automation/IT), and small-entity impact—including an official ICR notice itself requesting such comment. Score 0.5 when only one or two of these elements are addressed. Score 0.0 only when an ICR is clearly at issue but required elements are absent or dismissed.
134.orig_description: Identify PRA‑covered collections, issue required notices inviting comment on necessity, burden, and ways to reduce it (including automation/IT), and demonstrate consideration of burden minimization—especially for small entities—across specific ICRs.

135.best_description: Clarify Title IX coverage/authority: define sex discrimination (harassment/assault), govern access to sex-segregated programs/facilities including gender-identity protections, and address interpretive/state-federal conflicts. Score 1.0 for accurate, on-topic engagement with these Title IX issues; 0.5 for partial, vague, or one-sided engagement; 0.0 only when the comment engages a Title IX topic but is factually wrong or dismisses the protections. Answer NA whenever the comment never mentions Title IX, sex/gender discrimination, or sex-segregated facilities — including off-topic rants, unrelated-docket cover letters, or generic policy complaints; never score these 0.0.
135.orig_description: Clarify Title IX coverage and authority; define sex discrimination (including harassment/assault) and govern access to sex‑segregated programs/facilities, including protections based on gender identity; address interpretive/state‑federal conflicts and NPRM review topics.

136.best_description: Applies only to comments on FAA Class D/E airspace redesignation actions. Score NA if the comment never references airspace, NAVAID, or the proposed rule -- including unrelated topics, generic political rants, or boilerplate opposition/support with no rule-specific content; do not score 0.0 for these. Score 1.0 if the comment states a specific justification (e.g., NAVAID decommissioning/relocation), labels the action temporary vs. permanent/recurring, AND notes any post-NPRM change with rationale. Score 0.5 if one or two elements appear. Score 0.0 only if the comment substantively addresses the action but supplies none.
136.orig_description: Provide criteria/justifications for Class D/E airspace changes (e.g., tied to NAVAID changes), distinguish temporary vs. recurring actions, and document any post‑NPRM modifications/withdrawals with rationale.

137.best_description: Score whether the comment shows a regulated market of significant size with strong correlation/surveillance-sharing linkages sufficient to detect/deter manipulation in related spot markets, and that the ETP would not predominate price formation. Give 1.0 if size and surveillance linkages are both substantiated with specifics; 0.5 if only one is credibly addressed or evidence is partial; 0.0 only if the comment discusses ETP market structure, surveillance, or price formation but fails to demonstrate it. If the comment never mentions ETPs, regulated markets, surveillance, or price formation, answer NA, not 0.0.
137.orig_description: Demonstrate a regulated market of significant size and strong correlation/surveillance linkages sufficient to detect/deter manipulation in related spot markets, and that the ETP would not predominate price formation.

138.best_description: Apply only to comments on rules/permits that set enforceable, source-level emission/discharge limits or work-practice standards plus monitoring-recordkeeping-reporting (MRR). Score 1.0 for substantive engagement with applicability triggers, numeric/work-practice limits, MRR adequacy, or public access to compliance data. Score 0.5 if the comment argues a limit, monitoring, or transparency element matters, even without technical detail. Score 0.0 when squarely on-topic yet ignoring enforceability/MRR/transparency. Answer NA for generic opposition/support form letters, content-free attachments, and comments on non-permit rules (wildlife, fuel economy, disposal, land management, procurement, general opinion) — never 0.0.
138.orig_description: Ensure permits/rules have clear applicability triggers and enforceable emission/work practice limits (no unbounded discretion), require monitoring/recordkeeping/reporting sufficient for continuous compliance, and provide public access to compliance data.

139.best_description: Score only if the comment's visible text itself argues the agency's action is/isn't within its statutory authority, delegation, or judicial-doctrine limits (violates/exceeds the statute, conflicts with congressional intent, invokes major-questions or precedent). 1.0: clear, unhedged authority claim — citation not required. 0.5: claim is vague or hedged. 0.0: claim is confidently wrong, unsupported, or a bare authority buzzword unconnected to the statute. NA: values/policy opposition (even phrased as 'public trust' or 'managed for future generations'), naming a rule/Act with no authority argument, or letterhead/address-block/docket-citation text introducing an unseen attachment — formal or mandate-sounding language is not itself a claim; judge only visible argumentative text, never infer.
139.orig_description: Actions stay within specific delegations and adopt the statute’s single best reading (post‑Loper Bright), address major‑questions and other judicial‑doctrine constraints, respect binding precedent and prior practice, and avoid weak interpretive bases or unauthorized expansions of authority.

140.best_description: Score only if the comment engages CAA SIP/attainment-planning submission content: required components (RACT, emission statements, contingency measures), not-less-stringent/equivalency, enforceability, SIP consistency, or section 110(l)/approvability. 1.0 = submission meets these standards; 0.5 = partially meets or ambiguous adequacy; 0.0 = comment discusses SIP submission content but identifies it as deficient, non-stringent, unenforceable, or non-approvable. Answer NA if the comment does not address SIP/attainment-planning submission content at all — e.g., general opposition/support, unrelated topics, procedural complaints, or off-topic rants naming no SIP component or approvability criterion. Do not use 0.0 for off-topic comments; use NA.
140.orig_description: SIPs/attainment and planning submissions include required components (e.g., RACT, emission statements, contingency measures), maintain not‑less‑stringent/equivalency, ensure enforceability and consistency with the SIP, and satisfy section 110(l) and other approvability criteria.

141.best_description: Score whether the comment discusses employer heat-hazard prevention programs (triggers, monitoring/response procedures, feasible controls, training). Answer NA if the comment does not address workplace heat-illness prevention at all — off-topic submissions, comments on unrelated dockets/rules, generic political statements, or boilerplate cover letters with no program content. Use 0.0 only when the comment substantively engages this topic but describes or advocates a program lacking these elements. Score 0.5 for partial coverage (some elements present, others missing/vague) and 1.0 for a complete, specific program aligned with recommended standards.
141.orig_description: Employers implement written heat‑hazard programs with triggers, observation/response procedures, feasible controls, and training—aligned with recommended standards and best practices.

142.best_description: Score the full comment body; letterhead, addressee blocks, docket/RIN or 'Re:' lines, and 'see attached' are NEVER evidence, regardless of sender status. 1.0 needs BOTH: the commenter's own rule-specific data, study, legal authority, or stated professional credential, AND a specific requested action. 0.5: rule-relevant specifics or credentials present but only frames a problem/urgency without naming the requested action, or the visible text is just header/'see attached' with no substantive body. 0.0: personal life story, general/political opinion, or emotional narrative with no rule-specific data or credentialed critique. NA: off-topic or unreadable.
142.orig_description: Effective comments target specific proposed text, follow instructions/format, provide factual data and authorities, make concrete change requests, engage legal weight, and frame arguments to require agency consideration.

143.best_description: Score 1.0 when the comment cites the docket/rule title or unmistakably specific provisions/program under it, AND gives reasoning tied to that content — documented impacts, directly relevant experience, or critique of specific provisions. Score 0.5 when only one holds clearly. Score 0.0 when neither holds: generic policy opinions, rhetorical objections, personal anecdotes about the general topic, or self-description of an unrelated program with no stated link to the rule (e.g., 'see attached' plus unconnected background). NA only if the text isn't a rulemaking comment.
143.orig_description: Comments clearly identify the proceeding (docket/title), cite specific sections addressed, engage the issues the agency requested, and provide reasons for recommendations with sufficient detail to be actionable.

144.best_description: Comments identify governing legal standards and violations and cite controlling statutes/regulations with accurate CFR/USC section numbers when proposing or objecting to amendments.
144.orig_description: Comments identify governing legal standards and violations and cite controlling statutes/regulations with accurate CFR/USC section numbers when proposing or objecting to amendments.

145.best_description: Comply with NEPA EIS procedures: timely NOI/scoping, draft/final/supplemental EIS impacts/alternatives, public participation, and a compliant Record of Decision. Mark NA when the comment does not engage the EIS process itself — general policy opposition, unrelated rants, or other reviews like FAA Part 150 noise programs are NA, not 0.0. Give 1.0 when the comment substantively raises even one EIS procedural element (e.g., a scoping or impact-analysis gap); reserve 0.5 for vague/tangential mentions; use 0.0 only when it explicitly states a NEPA EIS violation or noncompliance.
145.orig_description: Comply with NEPA EIS procedures: timely NOI/scoping, preparation of draft/final/supplemental EISs with impacts/alternatives, robust public participation, and issuance of a Record of Decision meeting regulatory content requirements.

146.best_description: Apply only when the comment's visible text names and discusses a specific agency guidance document, sub-regulatory policy, or label/claim practice (e.g., 'free range,' 'humanely raised'). Score 1.0 if the text shows agency approval without a rule, disclaimer, or enforcement — including failure to regulate or verify the claim. Score 0.5 if it questions legitimacy without describing administration outside a rule. Score 0.0 if properly disclaimed or rule-governed. Score NA if no instrument is named, or the text is only boilerplate (cover letter, salutation, docket header) — never infer from letterhead.
146.orig_description: Policies in preambles/guidance do not create binding obligations; comply with OMB Good Guidance Bulletin; include clear non‑binding disclaimers and avoid substituting sub‑regulatory guidance for rulemaking.

147.best_description: Score only when the comment substantively engages with rules for handling public submissions: deception/false attribution (including questioning whether another commenter's name is genuine), verifying identity/consent for third-party submissions, prohibiting sensitive/PHI content, or posting/timeliness policy and exceptions. 1.0 = detailed reasoning proposing/endorsing safeguards. 0.5 = brief mention or passing skepticism about authenticity/attribution without developed reasoning. 0.0 = explicitly argues against such safeguards. NA = no mention at all — including ordinary comments merely listing the submitter's own name/contact/letterhead or 'see attached' notices.
147.orig_description: Govern public submissions to prevent deception and unauthorized attributions, require verification/consent for third‑party submissions, prohibit inclusion of sensitive/PHI, and clarify posting/timeliness rules and exceptions.

148.best_description: Score what the comment reveals about mass-campaign transparency and evidence integrity: sponsor/funder disclosure, campaign design/participation mechanics, fake/duplicate-comment abuse (including questioning another commenter's authenticity), and tracker exclusions. A letterhead or signature naming the submitting organization is NOT sponsor disclosure; require an explicit statement that the comment is part of an organized multi-commenter campaign. Score 1.0 for explicit substantive disclosure; 0.5 for partial/vague disclosure; 0.0 only if it names itself a campaign submission yet discloses nothing. NA covers any comment, including form-letter text, showing no mass-campaign signal.
148.orig_description: Mass‑comment campaigns disclose advocacy sponsors/clients, document design and participation, address scope/abuse (e.g., fake comments), and transparently state exclusions in trackers to maintain credibility.

149.best_description: Score whether the comment engages TILA/Reg Z rules for open- and closed-end credit: coverage/exemptions, account-opening/periodic disclosures, special mortgage and private education loan disclosures, post-consummation events, and advertising (finance charge/triggering terms, Closing Disclosure content). Answer NA whenever the comment does not discuss credit disclosure or advertising at all (e.g., an unrelated docket like immigration, tax, food/drug policy, fisheries, or employment) — never score off-topic text 0.0. Use 0.0 only for comments addressing Reg Z disclosure/advertising but wrong or incomplete; 0.5 for partial engagement; 1.0 for correct, specific coverage.
149.orig_description: Apply Truth in Lending/Reg Z rules across open‑ and closed‑end credit: coverage/exemptions, account‑opening and periodic disclosures, special mortgage and private education loan disclosures, post‑consummation events, and advertising requirements (including finance charge/triggering terms and Closing Disclosure content).

150.best_description: Score the ENTIRE comment, not just the letterhead—read past 'See attached file(s)', RE: lines, and addresses. Credit 1.0 for a pinpoint section/paragraph or a specific named docket/proceeding tied to a substantive point plus checkable support (data, studies, dates). Credit 0.5 when a specific office or proceeding is named but lacks a pinpoint, or is named only as background. Score 0.0 for boilerplate alone (docket numbers, RINs, RE: lines, addresses, salutations, 'see attached file(s)') or a named case with no tied verifiable point. NA only if no factual claim is made.
150.orig_description: High‑quality comments identify the exact provision(s) at issue (section/paragraph or pinpoint FR pagination) and support points with verifiable, accessible citations to primary sources or equally authoritative materials.

151.best_description: Score whether the comment text itself (not an attachment) gives the commenter's name and contact/affiliation, cites the correct docket/rule number, follows formatting/section rules, and excludes CBI/PII or other prohibited content. Missing identifiers or docket citation is a failure, not NA: score 0.0 when identifiers, docket reference, or formatting are absent, or CBI/PII appears. Score 0.5 when only some elements are present (name but no contact info, or vague docket citation). Score 1.0 only when name, contact/affiliation, and docket citation all appear with no prohibited content. Reserve NA for blank/non-comment submissions.
151.orig_description: Comments include required identifiers and contact details, correct docket references and organization by section, comply with formatting rules, and exclude confidential/CBI/PII or other prohibited content from public submissions.

152.best_description: Score identifying/structural metadata appropriate to document type. Agency notices/rules need: agency, action, summary, dates, addresses, SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION, subject headings, CFR parts, docket, RIN, accurate authority citation, proper signature(s) (incl. joint issuances), FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT, and IBR/referenced-materials statements. Public comment letters need only: docket/RIN/rule identified, submitter, date, contact — do not penalize comments for lacking FR-notice-only sections like SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION or effective dates. 0.5 = partial/ambiguous identification. 0.0 = expected metadata present but wrong or missing. NA = document type carries no such metadata by design.
152.orig_description: Rulemaking/notice documents include all required FR elements and metadata (agency, action, summary, dates, addresses, supplementary information, subject headings, CFR parts, docket, RIN), accurate authority citations/lines, proper signatures (including joint issuances), FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT, and statements on referenced/IBR materials and availability.

153.best_description: Score PRA/ICR compliance only when the comment's own visible text substantively discusses OMB paperwork content: control numbers/displays, ICR packages/supporting statements, burden-hour estimates, respondent definitions, or interagency/OMB clearance. Citing a docket titled 'Information Collection Activity' is not itself sufficient — a cover letter, 'see attached', or bare caption restatement caps at 0.5; if no PRA substance is visible, use NA. General complaints about cost, privacy/data storage, program timing, or patient/administrative burden unrelated to OMB paperwork are NA, not 0.5. Never score 0.0 for silence; 0.5=partial, 1.0=complete with visible burden/ICR specifics.
153.orig_description: Demonstrates PRA compliance: valid OMB control numbers and displays, complete ICR packages and supporting statements, accurate burden estimates and respondent definitions, and correct interagency/OMB clearance procedures and notices.

154.best_description: Score only comments engaging OSHA's proposed heat illness standard: applicability, evidence-based environmental/physiological heat triggers, required protections at baseline and high-heat thresholds (water, shade, rest, acclimatization, communication, emergency response), indoor/outdoor controls, and hazard alerting/training. Answer NA if the comment is off-topic OR is generic opposition/support (e.g., anti-government, tax-waste, "I oppose" rants) that names no specific rule element — do not infer engagement from tone alone. Use 0.0 only when the comment explicitly names or describes at least one specific element above, even while omitting or opposing it. Use 0.5 for partial coverage, 1.0 for substantive accurate engagement.
154.orig_description: Covers applicability, evidence‑based environmental/physiological heat triggers, required protections at baseline and high‑heat thresholds (water, shade, rest, acclimatization, communication, emergency response), indoor/outdoor controls, and hazard alerting/training.

155.best_description: Assess only text that engages FACA: when FACA applies, requirements/limits for establishing advisory committees, advisory-only scope absent specific authority, charter contents (mission, costs, meetings, duration), meeting closure determinations, and terms/renewals or interagency-committee applicability. Score 1.0 for accurate, specific engagement with these points; 0.5 for partial or vague engagement; 0.0 only if the comment substantively addresses FACA/advisory-committee topics but is wrong or unsupported. Answer NA if the comment is a cover letter, transmittal note, or attachment pointer with no visible substantive text, or does not discuss FACA/advisory committees at all.
155.orig_description: Determines when FACA applies; requirements and limits for establishing advisory committees; advisory‑only scope absent specific authority; charter contents (mission, costs, meetings, duration); meeting closure determinations; terms/renewals and interagency committee applicability.

156.best_description: Score whether the comment explicitly compares in-house versus contract-out (outsourcing) options for performing a function, with side-by-side benchmarking/metrics and a documented cost-comparison framework guiding the sourcing decision. Score 1.0 if both benchmarking and cost comparison are clearly present. Score 0.5 if only one is present, or the comparison is vague/partial. Score 0.0 only if the comment discusses in-house vs. contract-out sourcing but omits both. Answer NA if the comment never raises in-house vs. contract-out sourcing at all.
156.orig_description: Explicitly present in‑house and contract‑out alternatives with side‑by‑side benchmarking/metrics and a documented cost‑comparison framework to inform sourcing decisions.

157.best_description: Government‑wide sourcing policies defining inherently governmental vs. commercial activities, limits or prohibitions on A‑76 in specified contexts, and policy updates affecting competition posture.
157.orig_description: Government‑wide sourcing policies defining inherently governmental vs. commercial activities, limits or prohibitions on A‑76 in specified contexts, and policy updates affecting competition posture.

158.best_description: Assess engagement with broadband/BIAS regulation: Title II classification/forbearance, transparency/labeling and Section 222 privacy, bright-line/open Internet conduct rules, blocking/throttling evidence, universal service/accessibility, and federal-state preemption. Score 1.0 if it substantively argues at least one element with specifics or evidence. Score 0.5 if it briefly mentions such regulation without developed reasoning. Score 0.0 only if the comment names broadband/BIAS/ISP regulation but engages no element. Answer NA if the comment contains no broadband/BIAS-specific content at all—even if angry or opposed to regulation generally—including attachment-only stubs, wrong dockets, or generic complaints lacking broadband terms.
158.orig_description: Regulatory framework for broadband/BIAS: Title II classification and forbearance choices, transparency/labeling and consumer privacy (Section 222) obligations, bright‑line/open Internet conduct rules, evidence of blocking/throttling, universal service/accessibility, and federal–state preemption/interplay.

159.best_description: Score only comments discussing exchange listing standards for commodity-based trust shares or crypto-asset trusts: listing criteria, surveillance-sharing agreements, custody/operational safeguards, asset composition/staking policy, or options-listing procedures. Answer NA if the comment never addresses these listing-standard topics (e.g., unrelated dockets, tax/immigration/labor/agriculture filings, generic policy opinions) — never score such off-topic comments 0.0. Score 1.0 if it substantively engages and supports/meets the criteria; 0.5 if vague or partial engagement; 0.0 if it engages the topic but opposes or fails the criteria.
159.orig_description: Initial/continued listing criteria for commodity‑based trust shares (including crypto trusts), surveillance‑sharing with a regulated market of significant size, custody/operational safeguards, asset composition/staking policies, and procedural pathways for options listings.

160.best_description: Score whether the comment proposes, discusses, or rejects a specific content/instruction requirement under the Securities/Exchange Act and related forms/items (e.g., Reg S-K/S-X 202, 902, 1301; Form S-1; SPAC disclosures; loan portfolio disclosures; codes of ethics). First check topic: generic opposition, venting, or off-topic comments (wrong agency, docket, or subject like tax, immigration, agriculture) with no identifiable SEC-disclosure content are NA, never 0.0, regardless of tone or capitalization. Once the comment engages this topic, score 0.0 (no specific requirement, or rejects one), 0.5 (vague/partial), or 1.0 (clear, specific item).
160.orig_description: Content/instruction requirements under the Securities Act/Exchange Act and related forms/items (e.g., Reg S‑K/S‑X items such as 202, 902, 1301; Form S‑1; SPAC‑specific disclosures; loan portfolio disclosures; codes of ethics).

161.best_description: Score only comments discussing an agency's own APA/FOIA duty to publish, index, or disclose its legal materials (rules, orders, manuals, systems-of-records notices, international agreements, FISA opinions) or precedential use of unpublished agency material. 1.0: comment evaluates, praises, or requests changes to how the agency publishes/indexes/discloses these specific materials. 0.5: raises access/transparency concerns about such materials without a clear mechanism or scope. 0.0: comment names such legal materials but not their publication or accessibility. NA (default): no agency-publication topic raised — includes docket/letterhead boilerplate, personal/genealogical or historical-archive record requests, list-serve/notification-signup mentions, media/press access requests, and unrelated policy discussion.
161.orig_description: Agency obligations to publish and index organizational/procedural/substantive rules and legal materials (APA/FOIA), ensure precedential use only when properly published/indexed, and provide transparency for significant instruments (e.g., systems of records, international agreements, FISA opinions).

162.best_description: Score only comments discussing actual fee/billing content: charges, disclosures, refunds, billing-error handling, or rate/fee limits. Answer NA when absent -- general policy opposition/support, procedural cover letters (even if the docket name contains 'fee', e.g. 'Physician Fee Schedule'), unrelated topics (label marketing claims, immigration policy), or personal stories with no fee content. Never score 0.0 or 0.5 for NA cases. Score 1.0 for accurate, complete pre-billing disclosure of fee nature/purpose/amount/refundability with proper error resolution. Score 0.5 for partial/vague/ambiguous fee coverage. Score 0.0 only for explicit deceptive, hidden, or non-compliant fee/billing practices.
162.orig_description: Ensure truthful, complete pre‑billing disclosures; accurately represent fee nature/purpose/amount/refundability; follow billing‑error resolution procedures; comply with applicable rate/fee limitations; and prohibit deceptive fee practices.

163.best_description: Score using identifying AND substantive evidence, not full NPRM text. Score 1.0 when a tracking ID or formal caption ('In the matter of...Docket No.') co-occurs with rule-specific engagement — CFR/section cites, quoted regulatory language, or data rebuttal tied to a specific provision — or when a full formal caption appears alone. Score 0.5 when identifier is bare with personal narrative, general opinion, or background facts not tied to a provision, regardless of detail or emotion. Score 0.0 if identifiers misstate the notice. NA if addressing another commenter or unrelated matter.
163.orig_description: NPRMs must be published and include time, place, and nature of the proceeding, the legal authority, and a description of the substance/issues, together with customary FR sections (e.g., contacts, supplementary information) and required procedural details/findings.

164.best_description: Score only when the comment engages petition eligibility, categories (rulemaking, declaratory ruling, reconsideration/stay, test-procedure), prescribed form/content (factual/legal grounds, unfavorable information, statutory basis, proposed text), filing/timing, or Federal Register summary rules. NA: comment never raises petitions/petition procedure — general opinions, unrelated complaints, or an ordinary formal comment/cover letter (even on letterhead, citing a docket number) that doesn't discuss petition requirements. 1.0: substantively meets or correctly explains the prescribed content/procedure. 0.5: references petition process or is a formal filing but omits/misstates required elements. 0.0: addresses petitions yet violates or ignores stated requirements.
164.orig_description: Who may petition; petition categories (rulemaking, declaratory rulings, reconsideration/stays, test‑procedure petitions); prescribed form/content (complete factual/legal grounds, unfavorable information, statutory bases, proposed text/specific amendments); filing/timing; and required Federal Register summaries when applicable.

165.best_description: Score only comments discussing QHP certification network adequacy, Essential Community Provider (ECP) standards, or related information-collection burdens (e.g., SBE-EDE, standardized plan/certification reporting). Answer NA if the comment never mentions this docket's network-adequacy/ECP/ICR topic by name or substance, including generic anti-regulation rants, boilerplate opposition/support, or off-topic subjects (wrong rule, immigration, food labeling, vehicle recalls, fisheries) with no topic-specific content. Give 0.0 only when the comment explicitly names or references provider access, ECP, or the ICR but offers no substantive analysis. Give 1.0 for substantive, well-reasoned engagement; 0.5 for partial engagement.
165.orig_description: Substantive provider access and Essential Community Provider requirements for QHP certification and associated information collection burdens for demonstrating compliance (including SBE‑EDE and standardized plan/certification aspects).

166.best_description: Agency duties for rules with tribal implications: robust consultation and implementation plans, effective citation to trust responsibilities/statutes, avoidance of improper preemption, OMB/DPC consistency review, and funding considerations for direct compliance costs where practicable.
166.orig_description: Agency duties for rules with tribal implications: robust consultation and implementation plans, effective citation to trust responsibilities/statutes, avoidance of improper preemption, OMB/DPC consistency review, and funding considerations for direct compliance costs where practicable.

167.best_description: Scope/triggers for lobbyist registration, content of registration (including conviction disclosures), and public registers across jurisdictions.
167.orig_description: Scope/triggers for lobbyist registration, content of registration (including conviction disclosures), and public registers across jurisdictions.

168.best_description: Score only comments on Clean Air Act SIP dockets: §110(a)(2) elements, nonattainment/attainment or regional programs (haze/visibility, emission statements, §185 fees), or cross-state transport affecting NAAQS. Mark NA if the docket is unrelated (tax, USDA, fisheries, wildlife), or if the comment is generic content-free opposition/support (e.g., anti-government venting) with no air-quality- or rule-specific content — never 0.0 for these. Score 0.0 only when the comment addresses the rule's subject matter but misses a required SIP obligation. Score 1.0 for substantive engagement with a SIP element; 0.5 for partial/vague engagement.
168.orig_description: SIP submissions must address §110(a)(2) elements and applicable nonattainment/attainment and regional programs (e.g., §185 fee programs, regional haze demonstrations/visibility progress, emission statement programs) while ensuring non‑interference with NAAQS.

169.best_description: Score how correctly the comment applies GHS/CLP/HCS decision criteria for specific hazard classes (explosives; aerosols; chemicals under pressure; respiratory/skin sensitization incl. mixture rules; flammable gases/solids; water-reactive gas emitters). Give 1.0 if it accurately applies the relevant criteria; 0.5 if application is partial or ambiguous; 0.0 if it discusses these hazard classes but misapplies or misstates the criteria. Answer NA whenever the comment does not discuss GHS/HCS hazard classification at all — e.g., cover letters, boilerplate opposition/support statements, or unrelated topics.
169.orig_description: Apply GHS/CLP/HCS definitions and decision criteria for specific hazard classes (e.g., explosives, aerosols, chemicals under pressure; respiratory/skin sensitization including mixture rules; flammable gases/solids and water‑reactive gas emitters).

170.best_description: Assess whether controller–processor arrangements meet GDPR: required DPA terms (parties, subject matter, duration, data types/categories), processor duties (process only on instructions, sub‑processor change notices/consent, assist with DPIAs/requests, breach notification), audit/inspection rights, and controller obligations such as documenting personal data breaches.
170.orig_description: Assess whether controller–processor arrangements meet GDPR: required DPA terms (parties, subject matter, duration, data types/categories), processor duties (process only on instructions, sub‑processor change notices/consent, assist with DPIAs/requests, breach notification), audit/inspection rights, and controller obligations such as documenting personal data breaches.

171.best_description: Score whether the comment substantively defines Title IX covered conduct/contexts: sex-based harassment, off-campus conduct in a recipient's program/activity, or explicit inclusion of sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, pregnancy/related conditions, sexual orientation, gender identity. 1.0: gives concrete, specific detail on at least one element (e.g., a described incident showing why it applies) — multiple elements aren't required if one is substantive. 0.5: mentions an element only in passing or generically, without supporting detail. 0.0: engages this rulemaking but omits scope entirely. NA: doesn't address this rulemaking (unrelated regulation, or content-free opposition/support).
171.orig_description: Defines covered conduct and contexts under Title IX, including sex‑based harassment, applicability to off‑campus conduct in a recipient’s program or activity, and explicit inclusion of sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, pregnancy/related conditions, sexual orientation, and gender identity.

172.best_description: Score only comments that discuss Title IX grievance procedures: knowledge/response standards, hearings/cross-examination, training, sanction/remedy disclosure, evidence standards, timelines/delay notices, informal resolution, recordkeeping, or transition guidance. Answer NA if the comment does not engage this topic at all — general policy opposition, unrelated complaints, form/cover letters, or off-topic rants get NA, never 0.0. Score 1.0 when procedures described meet due-process/equity standards. Score 0.5 when the comment substantively raises Title IX process or safety concerns (e.g., a personal account) without full procedural detail. Score 0.0 only when procedures described fail those standards.
172.orig_description: Institutional Title IX procedures meet due‑process and equity standards: knowledge/response standards; hearing/cross‑examination where required; training; disclosure of sanction/remedy ranges; consistent standard of evidence; timelines with delay notices; informal resolution rules; recordkeeping/monitoring; and transition guidance across rule changes.

173.best_description: Protections for students and employees based on pregnancy, childbirth, and related conditions, including reasonable modifications, leave, lactation accommodations (time/space), and comparable treatment.
173.orig_description: Protections for students and employees based on pregnancy, childbirth, and related conditions, including reasonable modifications, leave, lactation accommodations (time/space), and comparable treatment.

174.best_description: Policies governing sex‑segregated teams, limits on categorical bans, try‑out requirements where only one‑sex teams exist, and treatment of transgender students’ participation consistent with Title IX.
174.orig_description: Policies governing sex‑segregated teams, limits on categorical bans, try‑out requirements where only one‑sex teams exist, and treatment of transgender students’ participation consistent with Title IX.

175.best_description: Score citation precision of legal authority FOR THIS action, not its subject. 1.0: exact statute+section, CFR/USC cite, formal authority statement, named program tied to this rule ('Clean Air Act §111,' '40 CFR Part 150,' 'the Part 150 process'), or docket/RIN paired with an explicit legal claim ('violates the statute'). 0.5: names the rule/settlement informally, no cite ('2015 coal ash rule'). 0.0: explicitly argues the agency lacks/exceeds authority or violates a law, names no source. NA: policy opinions, power complaints, personal stories, background, or docket/title used only as a header.
175.orig_description: Rulemaking documents clearly cite the specific statutory and regulatory authorities and relevant executive orders under which the action is proposed or adopted.

176.best_description: Comments identify the precise provisions addressed (e.g., FR page/column/paragraph or CFR section/line), state the docket/rule, include the docket ID, and anchor arguments to exact passages in the record.
176.orig_description: Comments identify the precise provisions addressed (e.g., FR page/column/paragraph or CFR section/line), state the docket/rule, include the docket ID, and anchor arguments to exact passages in the record.

177.best_description: Answer NA unless the submission exposes another person's private data without consent (SSN, medical record, address, identity), contains classified or discriminatory content, or attaches a fabricated/mocking name to any person — the commenter's own signature or a third party/prior commenter named in the text (e.g., doubting another commenter's name is real). Genuine self-disclosed name or personal history is normal, NA. Naming a government official is NA. Score 0.0 for unredacted PHI, non-consented identity use, or fabricated/joke identity for the commenter or another person; 1.0 only if redacted, anonymized, or consented.
177.orig_description: Submissions avoid prohibited content (e.g., classified or discriminatory content) and do not include sensitive personal information or unredacted PHI; identities are not used without consent.

178.best_description: Score comments on FAA airworthiness directives (ADs) specifying inspections, functional/general visual checks, mappings, or on-condition/terminating corrective actions for aircraft/parts. NA: no textual cue ties the comment to this AD or aircraft/parts inspection — generic anti-regulation rants or off-topic content (tax, drugs, food, fisheries, mining, vehicle recalls). 0.0: mentions the rule/AD/aircraft but shows no engagement with inspection/corrective-action content or docket-specific position. 0.5: generic/vague reference to the AD, not tied to specific requirements. 1.0: identifies the specific AD/docket or aircraft model with a clear position tied to inspection/check/corrective-action requirements.
178.orig_description: ADs requiring specified inspections, functional/general visual checks, mappings, and on‑condition or terminating corrective actions for affected aircraft/parts.

179.best_description: Tracks CRA disapprovals and explains legal consequences: nullification of the rule, requirement for new authorization to reissue a substantially similar rule, and continued enforceability of underlying statutory duties where applicable.
179.orig_description: Tracks CRA disapprovals and explains legal consequences: nullification of the rule, requirement for new authorization to reissue a substantially similar rule, and continued enforceability of underlying statutory duties where applicable.

180.best_description: Score only when the comment explicitly addresses the right to petition an agency to issue, amend, or repeal a rule, or discusses required petition contents (identity/interest, requested action, grounds/facts, certifications, APA §553(e) or agency-specific procedures). Score NA for ordinary comments on a proposed rule, cover letters, address blocks, or unrelated arguments that never raise petitioning — do not default to 0.0 for silence. Score 1.0 if petition content/procedure is covered accurately; 0.5 if partial; 0.0 only when petitioning is raised but handled incorrectly or incompletely.
180.orig_description: Public right to petition for issuance/amendment/repeal of rules and required petition contents/filing (identity/interest, action requested, grounds/facts, certifications, invocation of APA § 553(e) or agency‑specific procedures).

181.best_description: Score only if the comment itself makes a request for specific agency action (waiver, variance, exemption, declaration) as a petition/application/pleading. NA when only letterhead, address block, 'RE:'/caption line, or 'see attached' placeholder appears — even if unrelated substantive text follows — with no explicit request/grounds in visible text. Also NA for generic support/opposition or general rulemaking comments (analysis, evidence, criticism) not requesting specific action. 0.5: request/grounds referenced or implied but required elements (addresses, evidence, waiver docs, separate pleadings) unspecified. 0.0: addressed but inadequate/incorrect. 1.0: substantive, correct treatment.
181.orig_description: Procedural and content requirements for petitions/applications/pleadings (addresses, full statement of requested action and grounds with evidence, separate pleadings for distinct relief, documentation for waivers; avoid blanket requests).
